errors.english: bring him to mind in the manner in which you have heard of him
errors.why: The three objects of recollection are the Buddha, then (the Dharma) as heard, then the Saṅgha; the Tibetan says 'bring to mind in the aspect as heard', not the Buddha again 'as you heard of him'.

note: A careful, faithful rendering of the sequence of faith and the instruction on stabilizing it; only the middle object of recollection is drawn back onto the Buddha.

errors.english: Why is it necessary to state that it is not solitary?
errors.why: The Tibetan completes the opponent's demand from the previous side: 'one must state why it is not solitary', not a question about why it must be stated.

fix.find: Why is it necessary to state that it is not solitary?
fix.replace: [The opponent:] One must state why it is not solitary.

errors.english: Therefore, it has been stated as a logical consequence:
errors.why: This is a relative clause ('whatever consequence was stated, "why does a momentary thing not produce alone…"') whose predicate on the next side says it is thereby refuted; the English turns the opponent's prasaṅga into an asserted statement.

note: The momentariness argument is followed accurately; the opening fragment and the closing relative clause are mis-construed at the side boundaries.

errors.english: an offense of concealing an infraction
errors.why: ལྷག་མ is a saṅghāvaśeṣa offense; the phrase means a concealed saṅghāvaśeṣa offense, which is why the penalty (parivāsa etc.) follows.

fix.find: an offense of concealing an infraction

note: Sound rendering of the mentor's duties and the five-fold qualifications; one Vinaya offense class is lost.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
errors.why: ལྡན་པ here is the Vaiśeṣika quality conjunction (saṃyoga): 'number and conjunction are also impossible [for the six categories], since both are qualities and reside only in substances'.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are
fix.replace: number and conjunction (saṃyoga) are also impossible for them, because both number and conjunction are

errors.english: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
errors.why: The Tibetan is one expression, 'a row of palaces' and the like, an example parallel to 'the collection of the six categories'.

fix.find: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
fix.replace: it refers to expressions like "a row of palaces"

errors.english: Similarly, there is no differentiation among the collection of the six categories
errors.why: The Tibetan says that likewise, of expressions like 'the collection of the six categories', one should ask 'if there is no difference, how is it six?'; the English asserts the absence of difference as the author's thesis.

note: The infinite-regress argument about the nature of space is followed, but the Vaiśeṣika examples and the term saṃyoga in the last part are mishandled.

errors.english: Otherwise, there would never be any purpose [note: original: "don"] at all.
errors.why: དོན here is the thing and ལན་འགའ is 'occasional' (kādācitka): otherwise the thing would not be occasional, Dharmakīrti's standard argument.

fix.find: Otherwise, there would never be any purpose [note: original: "don"] at all.
fix.replace: Otherwise, the thing would not be occasional.

errors.english: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', is the anthill, the stock example of something emitting a smoke-like vapour (PV I verse).

fix.find: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
fix.replace: [note: Skt. śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', i.e. an anthill, which gives off a smoke-like vapour]

errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung (gomaya), the classic example of a heterogeneous cause from which lotus-plants etc. are seen to arise.

errors.english: Dependence is definitely not possible in that way.
errors.why: With the previous side's མི་, the sentence says that what does NOT depend on the help given by them cannot be restricted to that place and time; the English denies dependence instead.

note: The causal-restriction argument is broadly followed, but two stock examples (anthill, cow dung) and the key term 'occasional' are lost.

errors.english: by total residence, it is other than close residence
errors.why: ཡོངས་སུ་གནས་པ is the monk under probation (parivāsa), as the next side's ruling on a probationer shows, and ཉེ་བར་གནས་པའི་སྡོམ་པ is the upavāsa vow; 'total/close residence' and the note 'novice or lay vows' mislead.

note: The rule that a mostly-completed act counts as done, and the boundary case, are rendered correctly; the probation terminology at the end is literalised.
Faithful rendering of the Akṣayamati quotation and the argument on abandoning latent tendencies; the corrupt verse line is honestly flagged.

errors.english: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
errors.why: It is the opponent (གཞན) who, not understanding the intention, says the lemma 'the external ones…'; 'externalists' are not the speakers.

fix.find: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
fix.replace: The opponent, not understanding the intention, says "the external ones" and so forth.

errors.english: Because of the power of intense attachment
errors.why: ལྷག་པར་ཞེན་པ is adhyavasāya, conceptual determination, not attachment.

fix.find: Because of the power of intense attachment
fix.replace: Through the force of conceptual determination (adhyavasāya)

errors.english: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi
errors.why: དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ marks the root-text word 'that very'; the clause says the conceptual cognition, grasping what appears in [its own] cognition, seems to grasp a real thing; there is no 'tattva-buddhi'.

fix.find: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi
fix.replace: when it grasps what appears in the cognition (the root text's "that very")

errors.why: The gloss means 'those that are outside (other than) the universal', i.e. the particulars, not 'externalists'.

errors.english: the commentators and others offer a reply
errors.why: The author replies with the root-text words 'the explainers' and so on; the explainers are the topic of the reply, not the ones replying.

note: The svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya distinction at the end is right, but the dialectical frame (who says what) and two technical terms are garbled.
An accurate, well-annotated rendering of the refutation of a variegated conjunction in a painting or butterfly.

errors.english: Thus, if life itself is the (Pradhana), then that too becomes hollow.
errors.why: The clause says that pradhāna, being posited from the effect as potency, itself becomes hollow (སྲོག is likely a corruption); 'if life itself is the Pradhāna' is not in the argument.

errors.english: is described as the (Pradhana) Primary Matter being utterly hollow
errors.why: The quoted Sāṃkhya verse says that what comes within the range of sight is utterly hollow and without nature; the English makes it a description of what is seen as Pradhāna being hollow.

note: The dilemma on potency (manifest or other) is rendered correctly; the quoted verse and one corrupt clause are muddled.
